title: Tria capita ex opere quodam majori inedito de theoria lunae

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Euler is determining the Moon's true longitude from lunar-eclipse observations. On the previous page (§11–13) he showed the following. At mid-eclipse the Moon's longitude counted in its orbit, L, differs from the longitude of the shadow centre in the ecliptic, U = Sun ± 180°. The difference is U − L = (m+n+2k)·sin2x·tan²(ρ/2) / (g(n−m)) arcseconds. Here x is shadow (or Sun) minus node, ρ is the inclination, and n, m, k are the hourly motions of Moon, Sun and node in arcseconds. 1/g converts radians to arcseconds (≈206265).

§14: At mid-eclipse the Moon may be far enough from true opposition that terms depending on the angle η (an elongation-dependent inequality) are not negligible. So Euler proposes another approach: compute the Sun's and Moon's places not at mid-eclipse but at the instant when L equals U.

The relative motion in longitude is (n−m)″ per hour. The required time shift is therefore Δt = (U−L)/(n−m) hours, i.e. Δt = 3600(m+n+2k)·sin2x·tan²(ρ/2) / (g(n−m)²) seconds of time. This must be added to the time of mid-eclipse.

He splits this into two factors:
- The kinematic factor (m+n+2k)/(n−m)², taken from the hourly motions.
- The geometric factor (3600/g)·sin2x·tan²(ρ/2), tabulated for x = 0°–10° (and by symmetry 20°–30°, signs 0, V, VI, XI) with its logarithms.

Check at x = 1°, ρ = 5°17′: sin2° = 0.0349, tan²(2.6417°) = 0.002129, ×206265 = 15.33″ (the previous page's 15.3″), ×3600 ≈ 55,170, versus the tabulated 55,166.

At 10° the tabulated 538,930 is reproduced only if the slightly smaller inclination 5°16′29″ of the previous page's inclination column is used. So Euler lets ρ vary with sun−node distance, as in the previous table.

The logarithms check: log 55166 = 4.74167.

The argument is given here as Sun − node, rather than shadow − node as on the previous page. This is equivalent because sin2x has period 180°.

Typical size: with n = 2023″, m = 148″, k = 8″ the kinematic factor is 2187/1875² ≈ 6.2×10⁻⁴. Hence Δt ≈ 34 s at x = 1° and ≈ 5.6 min at x = 10°.

§15: Euler nevertheless says the earlier method (true orbital longitude at mid-eclipse) is safe. At that moment η, or its supplement, hardly exceeds 4′, so the η-dependent inequality is negligible. It is small compared with the unavoidable error of about one minute of time in the observed mid-eclipse, which corresponds to roughly half a minute of arc in the Moon's place.
errors: §15 as printed says an error of one minute of time in the mid-eclipse moment produces an error 'semissis minuti secundi' (half an arcsecond) in the Moon's place. With the Moon moving about 2023″/h (relative ≈1875″/h), one minute of time corresponds to about 31–34″, i.e. half a minute of ARC ('minuti primi'). This is likely a slip by Euler or the editors, or else the sentence refers to something else lost at the cropped margin.
Minor: the table entry for 1° (55166) is about 7 units (0.01%) below the value from g = 1/206265 and ρ = 5°17′0″. This is within rounding of the constants used; not a real error.

ideas.what: Reduction of the Moon's orbital longitude to the ecliptic, term sin2x·tan²(ρ/2), applied to eclipse geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Ptolemy/Tycho era tables; standard in 18th-c. lunar tables)
ideas.where_published: standard in Euler's lunar tables and theory (e.g. Theoria motuum lunae 1753/1772); unsure of the exact locus

ideas.what: Time correction to the instant when the Moon's orbital longitude equals the shadow's ecliptic longitude: Δt = (U−L)/(n−m), with tabulated geometric and kinematic factors
ideas.modern_name: reduction of mid-eclipse to the moment of opposition/conjunction in longitude
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard eclipse-reduction practice (Halley, Mayer, Lalande era)

ideas.what: Inclination taken as varying with Sun–node distance near eclipses (≈5°17′)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine computational table and time reduction for eclipse-based lunar longitudes. It is numerically correct and standard practice; no novel mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Header of the table: the right-hand column under 'Logarithm.' is the complementary degree column (30…20). The bottom labels are 'Subtrahe. | Logarithm. | Grad.' with signs V, XI. The top label '0, VI Sign.' applies to the left Grad. column.
Line 2 likely reads '...negligi possint, quo tamen calculus non mediocriter con[trahitur], expediet...' (margin cropped).
'error semissis minuti secundi' is as printed, but it is physically inconsistent (see errors).
